newsitem.title: GERMANY: Venezuelan oil company head sees firm oil price.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan oil company head sees firm oil price.

text.p: The president of Venezuelan state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela SA said on Wednesday oil prices will remain strong for the rest of the year.
Luis Giusti said the price of Venezuela's basket of crudes and refined products should average about $17 a barrel.
In 1995, Venezuela's oil basket averaged just $14.84 and at the beginning of 1996, PDVSA forecast an average of just $13.50 this year.

"(Oil prices) are probably going to be strong. We do not have a change in the fundamentals. The situation is temporary. This has been a non-typical year. Our slate will be around $17 a barrel," Giusti told Reuters.

Giusti, in Frankfurt with a government delegation seeking to woo European investors, said the current strong oil price had defied expectations of weaker prices when Iraqi oil exports return under a United Nations oil-for-food deal.
But the plan, which would send about 700,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Iraqi oil to the market, has been delayed by the military standoff between Iraq and the United States.
Giusti said low inventories of primary oil stocks was also supporting oil prices. Stocks of middle distillates, especially heating oil, are low in Europe and the United States.

"Everyone was expecting lower prices in the second half with the return of Iraq in the market. In general, stocks were kept low and you could see that with prices in backwardation," he said. Giusti said the fundamentals were strong despite reports of high production. Venezuela is said by oil analysts and several fellow OPEC delegations to be well over its OPEC quota.

"No matter what the volume is right now, I think it is healthy. It has really been the flexibility that kept the world from having a real supply crisis and maybe a real spike that would not be good for anyone," he said.

Two weeks ago in Caracas, Giusti said that if the average price for Venezuela's basket of crude and oil products ends the year at $15.60 a barrel, Venezuelan oil revenues would be at least $15.6 billion.

Using these figures, it appears that PDVSA expects to export about one billion barrels of crude and products in 1996 or a daily average of 2.739 million bpd, well over its OPEC quota of 2.359 million.
